items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: Then he had two sisters whom I knew very well, Ethel Goodman, what a lovely lady, Ethel and Ida.

ctx.x: Absolutely not. That’s why we’re here.

Benny Goodman actually never said hello to me. He would always say to me in Jewish, Monk, “you’re making a living?” And he would say to me in Jewish “a mach a leiben.” M-A-C-H-A I don’t know L-E-I-B-E-N I think. But he would always say that. And his brother would say that to me also, Harry, the bass player. A lovely guy. A great guy. Just passed away recently. Harry Goodman was like 95 years old. And he would always say © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

that to me. “Mach a leiben, mach a leiben.” You making a living? You know Benny Goodman came from a very, very poor family. And he came from a family, I think there was like ten children if I’m not mistaken. He was making a living playing his clarinet for his family at the age of maybe 13 years old. He supported his family. His father was a tailor. His father got killed by a truck in Chicago. And Benny Goodman’s first job, Tim, was doing an imitation of Ted Lewis. That was his first job, Monk, his first paying…
